newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt suspends wheat import plans for up to month.
newsitem.headline: Egypt suspends wheat import plans for up to month.

text.p: Egypt's main wheat importer said on Monday he was not planning to buy wheat for up to a month until health officials solve issues raised by an import ban on genetically engineered grain.

Egypt has issued a decree that it would require imports of commodities meant for human consumption to be accompanied by proof that genetic engineering was not used in their production. The decree said any imported grain or pulses must be accompanied by a certificate saying it has not been genetically altered.

"We confirm that we will stop plans for wheat importation for the next three to four weeks at least," Samir Shakankiri, vice chairman of the state's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC), told Reuters.

Shakankiri had said on Sunday import plans would be suspended for 15-20 days. Asked about the reason behind the extension, he said: "I am not satisfied yet. We are waiting for a radical solution to the problem.
"We used to watch the market to buy when prices go down. Even if we could get the wheat for free, we would not buy it because it would not enter the country without the certificate."

Shakankiri, whose organisation is the biggest wheat importer in Egypt, has said contacts were underway with exporting governments to see how they could issue such certificates. Egypt imports about six million tonnes of wheat a year from suppliers including U.S., France, Australia, and Argentina.
